posts.name: pwatson1974
posts.cooked:
Well, to get there, they've had to code 11 hero decks, some of whom have rules implications that need confirmation. Then they've gor 6 environments, even though they've been working on the Celestial Tribunal for a while. And then they've got 4 villain decks.

There are 22 hero cards to code up, and then to figure out how the heck they work with Completionist Guise and the Celestial Tribunal.

Then you've got OblivAeon himself and his three sides (Somewhat of a brand new mechanic needed), plue the Scions (also a new rule) and then you've got the fact that two environments have to be in play at once (which asks all sorts of questions) and rewrite a not insignificant part of the engine to accomodate all the rules for OblivAeon. It's a tough job and you can't start on it before playtesting finishes as quite a lot changed even late on in the playtesting. The fact that they're as far along as they are is pretty impressive from my view.

posts.name: bobbertoriley
posts.cooked:
I know Stuntman, Benchmark, and the Void Guard heroes were finalized/at the printers for a while now, so Handelabra has had plenty of time to get them put together. So, having them ready for when everyone starts having them in their hands makes a lot of sense.

As for the OblivAeon expansion, that didn't hit the printers until December or so, so they probably didn't get finalized content until that point. Even if they had nothing else to work on between now and then, I'd be frankly surprised if OblivAeon was done for the video game by the July timetable.

 

Not to mention Bottom of the 9th and One Deck Dungeon, which gave them something to work on while waiting for OblivAeon...like the rest of us. :)

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Yeah, none of the mini-expansion stuff except for Representative of Earth (which Handelabra's has had a long time to work on) and In Medias Res are tremendously complicated.  The only things delaying those should be >G's embargo date and their other work on One Deck Dungeon etc.

OblivAeon, on the other hand, is tremendously complicated.  Even more so than Vengeance, which took them a long time to get working.  And it's been finalized in print much more recently.  So I'd be happy to see it in 2018.  Hopefully we'll get the mini-expansion hero variants to tide us over until then.
